candidates.title: The generic Col and Row LP-index newtypes have zero consumers: the typed-address vocabulary their module doc describes is carried entirely by StateDim, CutSlot, BlockIdx, InCol and OutCol

evidence.command: git grep -n -E '\b(Col|Row)::new\b' 077dbe2c -- crates/ ; git grep -n -E '\b(Col|Row)::new\b|:\s*(Col|Row)\b|->\s*(Col|Row)\b' 077dbe2c -- crates/ | grep -v 'lp/indexer/index.rs' ; git grep -n -w Col 077dbe2c -- crates/ | grep -v 'lp/indexer/index.rs' | grep -vE '//[!/]' ; for s in StateDim CutSlot BlockIdx InCol OutCol Col; do echo -n "$s: "; git grep -l -w "$s" 077dbe2c -- crates/cobre-sddp/src | grep -v 'lp/indexer/index.rs' | grep -cv 'lp/indexer/mod.rs'; done
evidence.reading: Nothing in the repository constructs or names Col or Row as a type outside index.rs itself. The only non-declaration mention of Col in the crate is the re-export at lp/indexer/mod.rs:119; the only typed Row matches repo-wide are the unrelated cobre_io PriceStrategy::Row variant; the one remaining Col hit is prose inside a patch.rs doctest comment. Three tests in index.rs exist solely to give the two unused types a test: col_is_zero_cost_and_round_trips, row_is_zero_cost_and_round_trips and col_equality_is_value_based_not_identity. The five sibling newtypes declared in the same file are genuinely earned by 8, 5, 11, 2 and 3 consumer files respectively, so the finding is scoped to Col and Row alone. Neither carries #[allow(dead_code)] (both are pub and re-exported, so no lint fires to mark them reserved), neither appears in the mirror's Reserved-seam (Voice 4) class, and neither is on the prior-register roster, so this is not a sanctioned reserved seam. The module doc's own closing sentence concedes the seam these two were introduced for stays untyped: every type extracts its raw usize via get() for the solver-FFI seam, which stays usize-only per the infra-genericity rule.

candidates.fixShape: Delete the Col and Row declarations and their two impl blocks from lp/indexer/index.rs, delete the three tests that exist only to exercise them (col_is_zero_cost_and_round_trips, row_is_zero_cost_and_round_trips, col_equality_is_value_based_not_identity), drop the two names from the pub use in lp/indexer/mod.rs, and rewrite the index.rs module-doc sentence so the typed vocabulary it introduces lists only the types that exist: StateDim, CutSlot, BlockIdx, the InCol/OutCol role split and Boundary. Byte-neutral by construction, because the census proves zero production call sites, so no LP column, row, coefficient or bound moves; still assert the parity goldens in tests/parity.rs through tests/common/parity_hash.rs, the rank-invariance harness in tests/common/permute.rs, and mpiexec -n 1 versus -n 2 reproduction, and move no golden. The blast radius is the public API: lib.rs re-exports the module (pub use lp::indexer), so both names are public items of cobre-sddp and the deletion is a public-API removal with no in-repo consumer; the natural batching is the next public-API break, which the 0b carve-out of cobre-model already forces on this very module.

candidates.title: FphaRowRange is a zero-consumer public type whose module doc claims a production carrier that does not exist and whose row formula contradicts the live FPHA walker

evidence.command: git grep -n '\bFphaRowRange\b' 077dbe2c -- crates/ ; git grep -c 'FphaRowRange' 077dbe2c -- crates/cobre-sddp/src/lp/builder/template.rs crates/cobre-sddp/src/lp/builder/layout.rs ; git grep -c 'EvaporationIndices' 077dbe2c -- crates/cobre-sddp/src ; git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-sddp/src/lp/indexer/layout.rs | sed -n '1,9p;28,39p' ; git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-sddp/src/lp/builder/fpha_cursor.rs | sed -n '32,39p;54p'
evidence.reading: All eight repo-wide mentions of FphaRowRange are the declaration, its own Debug/Clone smoke test, two module-doc lines, the re-export at lp/indexer/mod.rs:120 and one prose cross-reference. No code anywhere constructs or reads the type. Two separate claims in the doc are false. First, the carrier claim: the module doc says these satellite types are produced by StageLayout and carried on its StageGeometry snapshot, which holds for the sibling EvaporationIndices (four production consumer files: builder/layout.rs, builder/mod.rs, builder/template.rs, lp/generic_constraints.rs) but not for FphaRowRange, which does not appear at all in builder/template.rs where StageGeometry is declared or in builder/layout.rs where StageLayout is declared. Second, the addressing claim: the documented formula start + k * planes_per_block + p is per-plant, while the live walker for_each_fpha_plane seeds fpha_block_start from layout.row_fpha_start() and its own doc states that the row-block base advances once per CELL, not once per plant, with that nesting called load-bearing for CSC row-sortedness. A reader who addressed FPHA rows through the documented formula would compute wrong rows for any multi-cell hydro. The type carries no #[allow(dead_code)] and no Reserved-seam rationale, and it is absent from the mirror's Reserved-seam (Voice 4) class and from the prior-register roster, so it is not a sanctioned seam.

candidates.fixShape: Delete the FphaRowRange declaration and the fpha_row_range_debug_clone_copy smoke test from lp/indexer/layout.rs, drop the name from the pub use in lp/indexer/mod.rs, narrow both module docs (the lp/indexer/layout.rs header and the satellite-types bullet in lp/indexer/mod.rs) to describe only EvaporationIndices, and repoint the sentence in lp/builder/fpha_cursor.rs that says it matches FphaRowRange::start at StageLayout::row_fpha_start, the value for_each_fpha_plane actually seeds its cursor from. Contract-first: the change touches no FPHA row emission, so neither the FPHA uses average storage section nor the Hydro-cell aggregation assumes one production map per cell section of .claude/rules/sddp.md is weakened; the cell-major nesting those sections rest on stays owned by for_each_fpha_plane, which is exactly why the dead type's per-plant formula must not survive as documentation of it. Byte-neutral by construction, since the type has zero construction sites and only prose changes accompany the deletion; assert the parity goldens in tests/parity.rs through tests/common/parity_hash.rs, the rank-invariance harness in tests/common/permute.rs, and mpiexec -n 1 versus -n 2 reproduction, and move no golden. Blast radius is the same public surface as the sibling finding, since lib.rs re-exports the indexer module.

positives.subject: Enum census over the 5b manifest — six enums, no one-variant enum
positives.why: git grep -n -E '^\s*(pub |pub\(crate\) )?enum ' 077dbe2c -- crates/cobre-sddp/src/lp/ returns exactly six declarations, and reading each body gives the variant counts: builder/columns.rs::BlockSlackFamily 2 (OutflowBelow, OutflowAbove), builder/columns.rs::CellSlackFamily 2 (TurbineBelow, GenerationBelow), builder/commitment_reconcile.rs::Reconciliation 3 (InBounds, Relaxed, Violation), generic_constraints.rs::ElementKind 9 (Turbine, Spillage, Diversion, Thermal, LineFwd, LineRev, Excess, ContractImport, ContractExport), indexer/index.rs::Boundary 3 (Incoming, Interior(usize), Outgoing), indexer/state_space.rs::StateRegion 4 (Storage, Lag, Buckets, CommitmentHold). The prompt's stricter crate-wide regex reproduces at the pin: 38 declarations across 30 files. No one-variant enum exists in this manifest, so the census yields no candidate. The two 2-variant slack families are real dispatch, matched in two shared fill helpers each in builder/columns.rs and driven from two-element descriptor arrays, not a hand-rolled boolean.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-sddp/src/lp/indexer/entity_index.rs — the ten entity newtypes
positives.why: HydroSys, HydroCell, ThermalSys, LineSys, FphaLocal, FphaCellLocal, EvapLocal, FillingTargetLocal, FloorLocal and AnticipatedLocal are ten repr(transparent) newtypes whose only methods are new and get, which is exactly the shape a speculative-generality sweep would flag. A per-type consumer census refutes it: every one has at least two production consumer files, the thinnest being FloorLocal and FillingTargetLocal at builder/columns.rs plus simulation/extraction.rs. The module doc also carries eight compile_fail doctests pinning the mismatch each type prevents and an explicit non-introduction paragraph stating that BusSys, NcsSys and ContractSys are deliberately NOT introduced because they would have no call site and ship as a dead type. That paragraph is the rule this lens would otherwise have to propose, already written down and honored.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-sddp/src/lp/indexer/storage_boundary_grid.rs::StorageBoundaryGrid and crates/cobre-sddp/src/lp/indexer/block_grid.rs::BlockGrid
positives.why: This answers the wrapper-layers-that-forward-without-deciding question for the indexer/builder seam. Three one-line forwarders exist (GenericResolverGeom::block_grid, GenericResolverGeom::block_storage_col, StageGeometry::block_storage_col) and each does forward without deciding, but each is a method on the data owner that delegates to the single owner of the offset formula, and each doc names the divergent hand-rolled re-derivation the delegation prevents. StorageBoundaryGrid has three consumers (builder/layout.rs, builder/template.rs, lp/generic_constraints.rs) and BlockGrid is consumed across eleven files. Raising these would be a false positive; the delegation is the design.

positives.subject: One-consumer sweep of the remaining indexer and builder seams in 5b
positives.why: Every other indirection in the manifest was consumer-counted and each has at least two, so the lens's one-consumer question yields nothing beyond the two candidates. indexer/range_cursor.rs::RangeCursor has two documented consumers (StageLayout's equipment chains and StateSpace's state-vector chain). indexer/cut_state_projection.rs is consumed across roughly twenty files. indexer/study_dimensions.rs::StudyDimensions has no methods but roughly twenty consumer files. indexer/hydro_cell.rs::HydroCellIndex has seven accessors and all seven have a production consumer, the thinnest being first_cell_of in builder/entries.rs and cell_of_bus in lp/generic_constraints.rs. builder/fpha_cursor.rs::for_each_fpha_plane has two named consumers, rows::fill_fpha_rows and entries::fill_fpha_entries, so the FphaVisit bundle is not a one-consumer abstraction. builder/delivery_ring.rs::DeliveryRing has three production consumers and its emit_shift_rows and emit_carry_rows are pinned as semantically distinct by a named regression test. builder/patch.rs::PatchBuffer's two counters are both read in production by training/stage_solve_prep.rs. builder/mod.rs::GenericConstraintRowEntry has no methods but six consumer files. indexer/anticipated_gate.rs::is_anticipated_decision_active is #[cfg(test)]-gated with a written rationale explaining that every production call site resolves its delivery stage through anticipated_resolution_for instead, which makes it sanctioned test retention rather than a dead indirection.

_needsHuman: Both candidates delete pub items that lib.rs re-exports through pub use lp::indexer, so each is a public-API removal even though neither has an in-repo consumer. CD-019 set the precedent of deferring superseded public API to the next public-API break. Should these two zero-consumer removals land now as ordinary cleanup, or be batched with the 0b cobre-model carve-out that relocates the indexer module anyway?
